subject: [PATCH v2 0/5] memcg: clean up memory.high enforcement

2026-10-31.patch_summary: This patch series cleans up memory.high enforcement by using a worker for kernel threads and remote charges, improving performance and handling edge cases such as reclaiming and sleeping during charging. It also forces charges from PF_MEMALLOC tasks before checking limits to prevent self-reclaiming and ensures that local user charges are handled correctly. The changes aim to provide a best-effort solution while maintaining the hard limit of memory.max for interrupts and swap. The patches modify various functions, including memcg_enforce_high(), to implement these improvements.

reviews.author: Michal Hocko
reviews.summary: Reviewer Michal Hocko noted that the current implementation of try_charge_memcg() can lead to a false event being triggered when reclaim operations need to allocate memory, and suggested checking the margin after the charge is forced instead.

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledges that their original approach was also racy, but notes that it had 'some additional issues' without providing details.

The author is addressing a concern about the patch's interaction with the `raised_max_event` mechanism. They acknowledge that this event cannot be removed, as it is also used by another part of the code (374f65b14819), and therefore forced charges will raise MEMCG_MAX again if it was already raised before reclaim.

The author addressed Michal Hocko's concern about the behavior of !mem_cgroup_margin() when usage equals max, explaining that it indeed triggers an event in this case.

Author acknowledges that the patch needs to handle events for all ancestors, agrees to keep their current version, and implies a fix is planned.
reviews.raw_body:
I actually tested your version as well i.e. after the charge. It is just
as racy and it has some additional issues which are inlined.

---

First, raised_max_event can't go. Since 374f65b14819 rejected charges use it
too, and without it forced charges that already raised MEMCG_MAX before reclaim
raise it again.

---

Second, !mem_cgroup_margin() is true at usage == max, so a charge that fits
exactly raises an event (unlike today).

---

Third, we definitely need a break here otherwise every ancestor at its limit gets
an event which does not happen today.

I want to keep my current version.
